hints: Linearise $y^n=Ax^3$ by taking natural logarithms of both sides.
Apply the power and product laws to obtain $n\ln y=\ln A+3\ln x$.
Regard $Y=\ln y$ and $X=\ln x$; rearrange into $Y=mX+c$ and identify why both $m$ and $c$ are constants.
walkthrough:
Take the natural logarithm of both sides of the given relation $y^n = Ax^3$:
$$\ln(y^n) = \ln(Ax^3)$$

Apply the product and power laws of logarithms:
$$\ln(y^n) = n\ln y$$
$$\ln(Ax^3) = \ln A + \ln(x^3) = \ln A + 3\ln x$$
$$n\ln y = \ln A + 3\ln x$$

Rearrange to express $\ln y$ explicitly by dividing through by the non-zero constant $n$:
$$\ln y = \left(\dfrac{3}{n}\right)\ln x + \dfrac{\ln A}{n}$$

Compare this equation with the linear equation $Y = mX + c$, where $Y = \ln y$ and $X = \ln x$:
- The gradient is $m = \dfrac{3}{n}$, which is a constant.
- The vertical intercept is $c = \dfrac{\ln A}{n}$, which is a constant.
Because $\ln y$ is related to $\ln x$ by an equation of the form $Y = mX + c$, the graph of $\ln y$ against $\ln x$ is a straight line.
